events.title: Public Gallery Tour
events.description: Solo and group exhibitions at Glyndor Gallery explore the dynamic relationships between nature, culture, and site. When exhibitions are on view in the spring, summer, and fall, Gallery Greeters lead public exhibition tours on Thursdays and Saturdays at 2PM. Visitors can expect an in-depth look at artworks on view in Glyndor Gallery and in the Sunroom Project Space, showcasing the work of both emerging and established artists in the unique context of a public garden.  Each tour lasts approximately 45 minutes. Drop-in event; no registration required. Today’s tour features current exhibitions. Questions? Please email us at information@wavehill.org or call 718.549.3200 x251.    Glyndor Gallery is wheelchair-accessible. There is an accessible, ground-level entrance at the front of the building with an elevator that provides access to the gallery level. The Sunroom Project Space can be accessed with an ADA-compliant ramp. The restroom on the gallery level is all-gender and ADA-compliant.

events.title: Summer Sports Experience: Basketball: Skills and Drills
events.description: Summer Sports Experience is an instructional youth program that teaches sports skills. Our knowledgeable NYC Parks staff train kids in sports such as basketball, ball hockey, kickball, flag football, pickleball, soccer, team handball, track and field, and volleyball. This program covers basic and more advanced techniques.  Summer Sports Experience is a drop-in program recommended for children ages 8-14. Participants can stop by for one or more sessions, but kids who stay for the whole program will get the most benefit from it. Occasionally a Summer Sports Experience program may be cancelled due to harsh weather or other conditions.Please note: We recommend that guardians accompany children participating in this program. Summer Sports Experience is not a childcare program, and NYC Parks is not responsible for the well-being of attendees. For more information, please visit nyc.gov/parks.  Contact accessibility@parks.nyc.gov or (212) 360-1430 for more information regarding accessibility.

events.title: Trees Count at Jennifer's Playground
events.description: Volunteer with NYC Parks for Trees Count 2025! At each event you will receive a tote bag with all the materials needed to count trees. Next, we'll provide a 30-minute training session that includes the basics of tree identification and how to measure and assess each tree. Using our Tree Census app, you’ll split up into different zones within the park to start counting trees! After completing your first training event, you are welcome to continue counting trees on your own in smaller parks across the city. For your comfort and safety, please bring water and wear closed-toe shoes to this program. To sign up a group of 10 or more volunteers please reach out to stewardship@parks.nyc.gov. Parking- There are two parking lots near the Visitor Services Booth, P3 and P4, where volunteers can park. For your comfort and safety, please bring water and wear closed-toe shoes to this program.

events.title: Volunteer Day: Bay 84th Street Community Garden
events.description: GreenThumb community gardens are developed, led, and cared for by dedicated volunteer gardeners who critically upkeep them as public green spaces.Bay 84th Street Community Garden, is searching for its community! We invite you to come visit the garden and help reimagine what this vital green space can be. We will be hosting an open garden day and volunteer session. Join us for hands-on community service open to all levels to help care for the garden, along with fun garden activities. We will have a kids' art station and teach visitors how to make their own smudge sticks to take home, using the same plant we will be weeding. This garden is creating space for those who are curious and willing to dig in. Join us! No prior experience necessary - beginners are welcome! GreenThumb will provide supplies and facilitation.This is a great opportunity to support and join a dynamic community space while learning about community gardens. Please wear comfortable, weather-appropriate clothing and bring water and snacks. Note: Some tasks may involve lifting heavy materials and extended periods of bending, squatting, and moving.Register here! Join our second event on August 15th here! Location: 3-22 Beach 84th St, Rockaway Beach, NY 11693For information about group volunteering, please contact Volunteer Program Coordinator, Olivia Navarro at Olivia.Navarro@parks.nyc.govThis event is co-hosted by NYC Parks GreenThumb. We are proud to be the nation’s largest urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.
